papers.title: Mito-nuclear incompatibility disrupts ACOX1/ACOX3-mediated mitochondria-peroxisome metabolic coordination in black soldier flies.
papers.summary: Using black soldier flies with heterologous mitochondrial genomes on a shared nuclear background, this study shows mito-nuclear mismatch disrupts mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, peroxisome biogenesis, and fatty acid metabolism via ACOX1/ACOX3. ACOX knockdown recapitulated energy deficiency, oxidative stress, delayed development, and reduced reproduction; reinstating ACOX expression alleviated lipid defects.

papers.title: Tumor growth going FAR with KRAS FARnesylation-induced phase separation.
papers.summary: This commentary highlights Wang et al.'s finding that farnesylation drives KRAS cytoplasmic condensation (phase separation), contributing to KRAS maturation. KRAS relays signals from cell-surface receptors at the plasma membrane, and the authors identify statins as candidate agents to overcome resistance to KRAS-targeted therapies.

papers.title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas of mouse soleus muscle: Unveiling single cell and subcellular heterogeneity in health and denervation.
papers.summary: This high-resolution spatial transcriptomic atlas of mouse soleus muscle with whole-transcriptome coverage resolves myofiber-level and subcellular heterogeneity, revealing hybrid myofiber states, mapping neuromuscular junction niche compartments, and characterizing fiber-type-specific stress responses plus spatially nonuniform damage-response gene domains along individual fibers after denervation.

papers.title: Bacterial chromosomal gene positioning is likely shaped by selection on both mean and growth-dependent expression.
papers.summary: Analyzing eight multi-environment protein expression datasets from three bacterial species plus E. coli promoter strengths, this study tests whether selection on mean expression or growth-dependent expression shapes chromosomal gene positioning near the replication origin. Both contribute moderately; combined they explain only a small fraction, partly offset by compensatory promoter evolution.

papers.title: Genetic analysis of epistasis between nucleotide excision repair and homologous recombination in the recovery of persisters after fluoroquinolone treatment.
papers.summary: In Escherichia coli, fluoroquinolone persisters recover by repairing antibiotic-induced DNA damage. This genetic analysis maps epistatic interactions between nucleotide excision repair (UvrA, UvrB, Mfd, UvrD) and homologous recombination (RecA, RecB, RecC), showing RecA's recombination and UvrD's helicase functions are required for persister recovery.

papers.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction drives metabolic reprogramming in Gitelman syndrome: insights from proteomics and isogenic modeling.
papers.summary: Combining quantitative plasma proteomics with a CRISPR-Cas9 isogenic SLC12A3 p.C421F 293T model, this study shows Gitelman syndrome features downregulated oxidative phosphorylation, TCA cycle, and fatty acid oxidation proteins; impaired respiratory chain complexes I-V, reduced ATP, compensatory glycolysis, oxidative stress, and aberrant lipid metabolism drive systemic metabolic reprogramming.

papers.title: Multi-gene biomarkers reveal spatial organization and subpopulation-specific damage response in biliary epithelial cells.
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq of mouse SOX9+ liver epithelium identifies four biliary epithelial cell subpopulations marked by minimal 1-2-gene 'metagenes', validated spatially by hybridization chain reaction FISH. Bile duct ligation suppresses subpopulation-specific genes and induces a proliferative subpopulation; heterogeneity persists in monolayer cultures.

papers.title: 18β-glycyrrhetinic acid ameliorates ifosfamide-induced nephrotoxicity by suppressing Wnt3a/IL-17A-driven inflammatory signaling, ER stress, and apoptosis while preserving ZO-1 integrity.
papers.summary: In rats, ifosfamide caused renal dysfunction, oxidative stress, inflammation, Wnt3a/IL-17A/ACT1/TRAF6 and Notch/HES1 activation, ER stress, apoptosis, and disrupted tubular ZO-1. Oral 18β-glycyrrhetinic acid co-treatment improved renal function and histology by suppressing these pathways while preserving epithelial junctional integrity.

papers.title: Itaconate metabolism in regulated cell death.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how the ACOD1-itaconate axis regulates apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis through mitochondrial metabolism, redox homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, and covalent protein modification. It discusses endogenous itaconate versus synthetic derivatives, itaconate-independent ACOD1 functions, and therapeutic targeting in inflammatory disease, infection, and cancer.

papers.title: Opportunities in cancer gene therapy: inhibiting MDM2 and restoring p14ARF as a means to activate p53.
papers.summary: This review examines the MDM2/p53/p14ARF axis in malignancies retaining wild-type TP53, where MDM2 overexpression or p14ARF loss suppresses p53. Gene-transfer strategies inhibiting MDM2 or restoring p14ARF can reactivate p53, promoting apoptosis, chemoradiosensitivity, and immunogenic cell death, positioning the axis as a context-dependent combination-therapy target.

papers.title: Multiple mechanisms cooperate to control PUF protein FBF-1 and FBF-2 accumulation in Caenorhabditis elegans germline.
papers.summary: This study implicates the ubiquitin-proteasome system in limiting accumulation of PUF proteins FBF-1/FBF-2 in C. elegans germline stem cells, identifies the FBF-2 C-terminal VR4 peptide as a degron, and defines a fourteen-gene network that constrains FBF levels in mitotic germline progenitors, some context-dependently.

papers.title: Decoding stem cell preconditioning as a novel strategy for improving its therapeutic efficacy in intervertebral disc regeneration.
papers.summary: This review covers mesenchymal stem cell therapy for intervertebral disc degeneration, where oxidative stress and poor cell survival limit engraftment in the avascular disc. Preconditioning strategies—including secretome and extracellular vesicle approaches—improve viability, reduce apoptosis, and enhance oxidative-stress resilience, though translational understanding remains incomplete.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization and Cophylogenetic Relationships between Crassicauda spp. (Nematoda: Spirurida) and Cetaceans of the Northwest Atlantic.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Using COI, ITS2, and SSU markers from northwest Atlantic specimens plus GenBank sequences, this study resolves eleven Crassicauda nematode species infecting fifteen cetacean species, revealing cryptic diversity. Distance-based analyses detect significant cophylogenetic signal while event-based methods show incongruence, supporting colonization and diversification within odontocetes, notably delphinids.

papers.title: The ubiquitin system in normal and infected germinal center B cells.
papers.summary: This review describes how ubiquitin pathways regulate proliferation, DNA damage responses, apoptosis, and differentiation in germinal center B cells, and how oncogenic gammaherpesviruses co-opt these mechanisms to establish latency and eventually drive lymphomagenesis, highlighting shared and divergent control circuits relevant to antiviral immunity and cancer.

papers.title: Proteomic analysis reveals a metabolic switch and cellular remodelling in pancreatic-like cell spheroids cocultured with hepatocyte-like cells using an interconnected liver-pancreas-on-chip system.
papers.summary: An organ-on-chip device co-cultures human iPSC-derived pancreatic-like spheroids with hepatocyte-like cells. Proteomics reveals a metabolic switch: co-culture increases extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory, and pro-apoptotic proteins, while monocultures show higher fatty-acid metabolism, glycolysis, and citrate cycle proteins, with moderate changes in pancreatic hormone secretion.

papers.title: A comprehensive full-length transcriptome landscape of cigarette smoke-exposed HASMCs reveals extensive remodeling of mRNA isoforms and regulatory networks.
papers.summary: Oxford nanopore long-read sequencing of cigarette smoke extract-treated human aortic smooth muscle cells reveals 11,222 novel transcripts and extensive isoform remodeling: upregulated ferroptosis and cell-division transcripts, downregulated oxidative phosphorylation and glutathione metabolism, 3'UTR remodeling via alternative polyadenylation, and altered splicing of cell-cycle regulators.

papers.title: Serum Cystatin 4 combined with routine clinical laboratory indicators: A support vector machine diagnostic model for early screening of gastrointestinal tumors.
papers.summary: Using 38 laboratory variables from 214 gastrointestinal tumor patients and 130 controls, feature selection identified seven core variables including serum Cystatin 4. A support vector machine model achieved AUC 0.85 with 95.4% sensitivity but modest specificity (61.5%), positioning it as an auxiliary high-risk stratification tool pending external validation.

papers.title: SpectralTCN: A multi-resolution wavelet gating network for vibration-based structural damage detection.
papers.summary: SpectralTCN augments a temporal convolutional network with a wavelet gating module performing learnable multi-resolution filtering that preserves both timing and spectral location of damage-induced anomalies. On the z24 bridge and My Thuan bridge benchmarks it achieved 92.2% and 92.1% mean accuracy, outperforming ten baselines and four ablations.

papers.title: Protodioscin mitigates cyclophosphamide-induced renal toxicity in HEK-293 cells by regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress, antioxidant defense, and apoptotic pathways.
papers.summary: In HEK-293 kidney cells exposed to cyclophosphamide, protodioscin (5-10 µM) reduced BAX and cleaved caspase-3, increased BCL-2, attenuated ATF6/PERK/GRP78/CHOP ER-stress signaling, increased catalase, GPx, GSH, and SOD, and lowered KIM-1, cystatin C, MDA, and nitric oxide, indicating renoprotection via anti-apoptotic, ER-stress, and antioxidant mechanisms.

papers.title: Sex-based differences in the gut-metabolism axis in aging and Nrf2-deficient mice.
papers.summary: Comparing aged wild-type and Nrf2 knockout mice of both sexes, this study found glucose tolerance impaired mainly in aged male Nrf2-KO mice, hepatic and adipose lipid accumulation increased with aging and Nrf2 deficiency, and female Nrf2-KO mice showed reduced gut microbiota α-diversity, highlighting sex-dimorphic effects on the gut-metabolism axis.

papers.title: Using ovine eyes as a readily available source for the isolation and 2D or 3D cultivation of uveal melanocytes.
papers.summary: This protocol establishes ovine eyes as a readily available source for isolating uveal melanocytes, confirmed by melanin production and pigmentation-pathway gene expression. Cells grow better in smooth muscle growth medium than modified F12, can be cryopreserved and recultured, and form 3D spheroids, enabling scalable uveal melanocyte research.

papers.title: PAK4-targeting PROTAC inhibits bladder cancer cell proliferation.
papers.summary: PAK4 is highly expressed in bladder cancer tissues. PAK4 knockout and a peptide PROTAC (PPD) both inhibited the ERK1/2-CDK4 pathway, blocked G1-to-S cell-cycle transition, and induced caspase-3-mediated apoptosis; both significantly suppressed bladder cancer growth in vivo, supporting PAK4 degradation as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA-seq and machine learning identify HMGN2 as a lactylation-associated hub gene in heart failure.
papers.summary: Integrating single-cell RNA-seq from failing and non-failing human hearts, this study shows elevated lactylation activity in heart failure, highest in fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells. Machine learning identifies HMGN2 as the most consistent hub gene, linked to immune-inflammatory signaling, and in vivo validation shows increased HMGN2 in pressure-overload mice.

papers.title: Comparative oligo-FISH validates genome assemblies and delivers a precise karyotype for Lens Mill. species.
papers.summary: Developing cross-species oligo-FISH probes from synteny analysis between cultivated lentil and six wild relatives, this study generates distinct red-green probe patterns for each Lens chromosome, enabling robust karyotyping that validates genome assemblies, confirms structural rearrangements, and supports species' pan-genome and plant genome assembly projects.

papers.title: Beyond digital investment: How value embedding modes shape ESG performance in energy-intensive firms.
papers.summary: Using panel data from China's energy-intensive listed firms (2011-2024), this study proposes a 'value embedding mode' framework: digital transformation improves ESG performance mainly through information-embedded pathways improving the external information environment, while asset-embedded green-innovation mediation is not robustly supported given capital-intensive, slow asset-renewal structures.

papers.title: Web-based Cellpose‑SAM segmentation enables quantification of cross-sectional area in formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded skeletal muscle sections stained with hematoxylin and eosin.
papers.summary: This workflow applies web-based Cellpose-SAM segmentation to H&E- or toluidine blue-stained FFPE skeletal muscle sections, enabling myofiber cross-sectional area quantification without cryosections or immunofluorescence. In mouse soleus, sciatic nerve crush showed a characteristic left-shifted CSA distribution versus sham, consistent with rapid denervation atrophy.

papers.title: Chromogranin B acts as a neuronal paracrine factor to trigger oligodendrocyte apoptosis.
papers.summary: This study shows chromogranin B, normally a secretory granule protein secreted by neurons, triggers apoptosis in mature oligodendrocytes and precursor cells. Anti-CHGB antibody neutralizes this effect, and neuron-oligodendrocyte co-cultures confirm endogenous neuronal CHGB promotes oligodendrocyte death, implicating neuronal secretory factors in demyelination.

papers.title: Erratum.
papers.summary: This erratum corrects Figure 4C of the 2017 article on angiotensin II/AT1/AT2-mediated cAMP-dependent PKA pathway effects on osteoporosis, replacing an incorrectly placed TRAP-staining image and blank control due to image-naming errors, while reporting that quantitative cell counting confirmed the original conclusions remain supported.

papers.title: Propolis ameliorates cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity via activation of Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway in rats.
papers.summary: In rats given cisplatin (5 mg/kg), oral propolis restored renal function, antioxidant status, and histological structure while reducing lipid peroxidation, IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, and caspase-3, and increasing Nrf2/HO-1 kidney expression. LC-MS characterized phenolic acids and flavonoids likely contributing to these nephroprotective effects.

papers.title: The C-terminal truncated splicing variant of NK1R negatively modulates substance P-stimulated NK1R signaling.
papers.summary: Using NanoBiT and co-immunoprecipitation, this study shows the truncated NK1R splice variant NK1S dimerizes with full-length NK1L, impairing Gαq coupling and calcium mobilization while enhancing β-arrestin1 recruitment, shifting signaling bias toward β-arrestin pathways and suppressing NK1L-mediated cell migration in A549 cells.

papers.title: The C-terminal domain of yeast Arginyltransferase1 is essential for its catalytic activity.
papers.summary: In budding yeast, the C-terminal domain of arginyltransferase 1 (Ate1) is essential for enzyme stability, catalytic activity, and Ate1-mediated cell death. Co-expression of separated N- and C-terminal halves fails to reconstitute activity, and mutating conserved N-terminal cofactor-binding residues also abolishes function, underscoring structural interdependence.

papers.title: Marine Microalgal Genes: Unlocking a New Era of Sustainable High Value PUFA Production for Neuroprotective Applications.
papers.summary: This review examines marine microalgae as sources of polyunsaturated fatty acid biosynthetic genes, focusing on desaturase and elongase enzymes, omics analyses, and synthetic biology strategies for heterologous expression in terrestrial oilseed crops and microbial hosts toward sustainable, scalable EPA/DHA production for neuroprotective applications.

papers.title: The complete mitochondrial genome of Malaysian Macrobrachium rosenbergii (De Man, 1879) and its phylogenetic relationship among Palaemonidae.
papers.summary: This study sequences the complete mitochondrial genome (15,332 bp) of Malaysian giant freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii, comprising 13 protein-coding, 22 tRNA, and two rRNA genes with A+T bias. Maximum-likelihood phylogenetics of 13 protein-coding genes places the Perak specimen in a strongly supported M. rosenbergii clade among Palaemonidae.
